dataset.name: Timeseries Unlabeled and Labeled Photos, Modeled Stream Elevation, and (Meta)Data of Variably Inundated Streams Across The Yakima River Basin, Washington, United States (v2)
description: This dataset is associated with the “River Monitoring Photos” (RMP) study and subsequent manuscript (Bao et al. 2025. Monitoring river flow status using low-cost wildlife camera and image segmentation artificial intelligence doi: 10.1016/j.envsoft.2025.106715). Game camera timeseries photos were collected to evaluate stream variable inundation via changes in width. A subset of photos was labeled for training the YOLOv8 and Mask2Former models and used to segment water surface fractions from all the game camera photos.

This data package was originally published in March 2024. It was updated in October 2025 (v2) to add additional photos and files associated with the manuscript (i.e., processed data, labeled photos, and trained models).
For details on how to navigate data packages generated by this project, see https://data.ess-dive.lbl.gov/portals/PNNLRiverCorridorSFA/About.

In addition to a readme, this data package also includes two file-level metadata (FLMD) files that describes each file and two data dictionaries (DD) that describe all column/row headers and variable definitions.

This dataset is comprised of (1) file-level metadata; (2) data dictionary; (3) readme; (4) field metadata; and (5) folders containing game camera photos and manuscript-associated files. Each Yakima River Basin site has a folder that contains subfolders for each month photos were collected. There is also a folder for files associated with the manuscript which has subfolders for labeled data, trained models, Yakima River Basin site water surface fractions, and USGS site water surface fractions. All files are .csv, .json, .txt, .yaml, .pth, .pt, or .pdf.

We thank the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation Tribal Council and Yakama Nation Fisheries for working with us to facilitate sample collection and optimization of data usage according to their values and worldview.

measurementTechnique: Game cameras without cellular capabilities (“no-cell”; SPYPOINT FLEX Cellular Train Camera) and with cellular capabilities (“cell”; CAMPARK Wifi Trail Camera) were deployed on a tripod at six sites across the Yakima River Basin (YRB). To install each camera, a location along the riverbank with a clear view spanning bank to bank was chosen, then positioned the lens toward the water channel. Depending on site conditions (vegetation and view), the cameras were mounted on a tree trunk, a tripod, or a tripod secured to a tree trunk. Cameras were fastened using straps and locked wire ropes to ensure security, accessibility, and discretion from public view. The cameras were set to take one photo at a regular time interval (i.e. every hour). Some cameras/sites had 5 photos taken at a time (each photo in the burst is denoted with “-#” at the end of the file name). During the first deployment at a site or any subsequent changes in the position of the camera, a reference photo was taken (denoted by “RefPhoto” in the file name). In the reference photo, the field staff are holding a tape measure extended two meters approximately 10 meters away from the camera. Photos from the cameras were downloaded approximately every 2 weeks. Set in time-lapse mode, the cameras were programmed to capture images every four hours. For the manuscript, a subset of photos was labeled using LabelMe. The labeled photos were used for training models YOLOv8 and Mask2Former to segment water surface from background.
